    OPT   Est. Speedup: 44.62%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 13.1 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant     
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 44.6% of the total average of 29.3 cycles between issuing two instructions.       
    ----- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

          on each stall reason.

    OPT   Est. Speedup: 51.14%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 16.4 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant     
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 51.1% of the total average of 32.1 cycles between issuing two instructions.       
    ----- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

          on each stall reason.

    OPT   Est. Speedup: 0.008469%                                                                                       
          Instructions are executed in warps, which are groups of 32 threads. Optimal instruction throughput is         
          achieved if all 32 threads of a warp execute the same instruction. The chosen launch configuration, early     
          thread completion, and divergent flow control can significantly lower the number of active threads in a warp  
          per cycle. This workload achieves an average of 1.0 threads being active per cycle. This is further reduced   
          to 0.9 threads per warp due to predication. The compiler may use predication to avoid an actual branch.       
          Instead, all instructions are scheduled, but a per-thread condition code or predicate controls which threads  
          execute the instructions. Try to avoid different execution paths within a warp when possible.

    OPT   Est. Speedup: 39.84%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 8.2 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant      
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 39.8% of the total average of 20.6 cycles between issuing two instructions.       
    ----- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    INF   Check the Warp Stall Sampling (All Samples) table for the top stall locations in your source based on         
          sampling data. The Kernel Profiling Guide                                                                     
          (https://docs.nvidia.com/nsight-compute/ProfilingGuide/index.html#metrics-reference) provides more details    
          on each stall reason.                                                                                         
    ----- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    OPT   Est. Speedup: 0.1206%                                                                                         
          Instructions are executed in warps, which are groups of 32 threads. Optimal instruction throughput is         
          achieved if all 32 threads of a warp execute the same instruction. The chosen launch configuration, early     
          thread completion, and divergent flow control can significantly lower the number of active threads in a warp  
          per cycle. This workload achieves an average of 3.0 threads being active per cycle. This is further reduced   
          to 2.9 threads per warp due to predication. The compiler may use predication to avoid an actual branch.       
          Instead, all instructions are scheduled, but a per-thread condition code or predicate controls which threads  
          execute the instructions. Try to avoid different execution paths within a warp when possible.

    OPT   Est. Speedup: 47.5%                                                                                           
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 8.9 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant      
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 47.5% of the total average of 18.7 cycles between issuing two instructions.

          are the subset of active warps that are ready to issue their next instruction. Every cycle with no eligible   
          warp results in no instruction being issued and the issue slot remains unused. To increase the number of      
          eligible warps, reduce the time the active warps are stalled by inspecting the top stall reasons on the Warp

    OPT   Est. Speedup: 43.03%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 11.6 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant     
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 43.0% of the total average of 26.9 cycles between issuing two instructions.       
    ----- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    OPT   Est. Speedup: 30.74%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 8.3 cycles being stalled waiting for a scoreboard dependency on 
          a L1TEX (local, global, surface, texture) operation. Find the instruction producing the data being waited     
          upon to identify the culprit. To reduce the number of cycles waiting on L1TEX data accesses verify the        
          memory access patterns are optimal for the target architecture, attempt to increase cache hit rates by        
          increasing data locality (coalescing), or by changing the cache configuration. Consider moving frequently     
          used data to shared memory. This stall type represents about 30.7% of the total average of 26.9 cycles        
          between issuing two instructions.

    OPT   Est. Speedup: 43.3%                                                                                           
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 10.1 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant     
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 43.3% of the total average of 23.2 cycles between issuing two instructions.       
    ----- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    OPT   Est. Speedup: 31.66%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 7.3 cycles being stalled waiting for a scoreboard dependency on 
          a L1TEX (local, global, surface, texture) operation. Find the instruction producing the data being waited     
          upon to identify the culprit. To reduce the number of cycles waiting on L1TEX data accesses verify the        
          memory access patterns are optimal for the target architecture, attempt to increase cache hit rates by        
          increasing data locality (coalescing), or by changing the cache configuration. Consider moving frequently     
          used data to shared memory. This stall type represents about 31.7% of the total average of 23.2 cycles        
          between issuing two instructions.

    OPT   Est. Speedup: 43.67%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 10.2 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant     
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 43.7% of the total average of 23.3 cycles between issuing two instructions.       
    ----- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    OPT   Est. Speedup: 32.13%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 7.5 cycles being stalled waiting for a scoreboard dependency on 
          a L1TEX (local, global, surface, texture) operation. Find the instruction producing the data being waited     
          upon to identify the culprit. To reduce the number of cycles waiting on L1TEX data accesses verify the        
          memory access patterns are optimal for the target architecture, attempt to increase cache hit rates by        
          increasing data locality (coalescing), or by changing the cache configuration. Consider moving frequently     
          used data to shared memory. This stall type represents about 32.1% of the total average of 23.3 cycles        
          between issuing two instructions.

    OPT   Est. Speedup: 44.88%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 11.7 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant     
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 44.9% of the total average of 26.0 cycles between issuing two instructions.

    OPT   Est. Speedup: 46.65%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 15.3 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant     
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 46.6% of the total average of 32.7 cycles between issuing two instructions.       
    ----- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    OPT   Est. Speedup: 32.05%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 10.5 cycles being stalled waiting for a scoreboard dependency   
          on a L1TEX (local, global, surface, texture) operation. Find the instruction producing the data being waited  
          upon to identify the culprit. To reduce the number of cycles waiting on L1TEX data accesses verify the        
          memory access patterns are optimal for the target architecture, attempt to increase cache hit rates by        
          increasing data locality (coalescing), or by changing the cache configuration. Consider moving frequently     
          used data to shared memory. This stall type represents about 32.1% of the total average of 32.7 cycles        
          between issuing two instructions.

    OPT   Est. Speedup: 46.49%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 11.4 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant     
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 46.5% of the total average of 24.5 cycles between issuing two instructions.       
    ----- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

          on each stall reason.

    OPT   Est. Speedup: 34.05%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 5.2 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant      
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 34.1% of the total average of 15.4 cycles between issuing two instructions.

    OPT   Est. Speedup: 63.6%                                                                                           
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 12.7 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant     
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 63.6% of the total average of 20.0 cycles between issuing two instructions.       
    ----- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    INF   Check the Warp Stall Sampling (All Samples) table for the top stall locations in your source based on         
          sampling data. The Kernel Profiling Guide                                                                     
          (https://docs.nvidia.com/nsight-compute/ProfilingGuide/index.html#metrics-reference) provides more details    
          on each stall reason.                                                                                         
    ----- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    OPT   Est. Speedup: 0.01185%                                                                                        
          Instructions are executed in warps, which are groups of 32 threads. Optimal instruction throughput is         
          achieved if all 32 threads of a warp execute the same instruction. The chosen launch configuration, early     
          thread completion, and divergent flow control can significantly lower the number of active threads in a warp  
          per cycle. This workload achieves an average of 1.0 threads being active per cycle. This is further reduced   
          to 0.9 threads per warp due to predication. The compiler may use predication to avoid an actual branch.       
          Instead, all instructions are scheduled, but a per-thread condition code or predicate controls which threads  
          execute the instructions. Try to avoid different execution paths within a warp when possible.

    OPT   Est. Speedup: 31.8%                                                                                           
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 9.9 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant      
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 31.8% of the total average of 31.2 cycles between issuing two instructions.

    OPT   Est. Speedup: 32.17%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 5.6 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant      
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 32.2% of the total average of 17.6 cycles between issuing two instructions.

          On average, each warp of this workload spends 7.1 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant      
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 35.5% of the total average of 19.9 cycles between issuing two instructions.

          per cycle. This workload achieves an average of 24.5 threads being active per cycle. This is further reduced  
          to 23.0 threads per warp due to predication. The compiler may use predication to avoid an actual branch.      
          Instead, all instructions are scheduled, but a per-thread condition code or predicate controls which threads  
          execute the instructions. Try to avoid different execution paths within a warp when possible.

    OPT   Est. Speedup: 71.54%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 26.2 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant     
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 71.5% of the total average of 36.6 cycles between issuing two instructions.       
    ----- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

          (https://docs.nvidia.com/nsight-compute/ProfilingGuide/index.html#metrics-reference) provides more details    
          on each stall reason.                                                                                         
    ----- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    OPT   Est. Speedup: 0.005707%                                                                                       
          Instructions are executed in warps, which are groups of 32 threads. Optimal instruction throughput is         
          achieved if all 32 threads of a warp execute the same instruction. The chosen launch configuration, early     
          thread completion, and divergent flow control can significantly lower the number of active threads in a warp  
          per cycle. This workload achieves an average of 1.0 threads being active per cycle. This is further reduced   
          to 0.9 threads per warp due to predication. The compiler may use predication to avoid an actual branch.       
          Instead, all instructions are scheduled, but a per-thread condition code or predicate controls which threads  
          execute the instructions. Try to avoid different execution paths within a warp when possible.

    OPT   Est. Speedup: 72%                                                                                             
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 21.1 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant     
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 72.0% of the total average of 29.3 cycles between issuing two instructions.       
    ----- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

          on each stall reason.                                                                                         
    ----- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    OPT   Est. Speedup: 0.01108%                                                                                        
          Instructions are executed in warps, which are groups of 32 threads. Optimal instruction throughput is         
          achieved if all 32 threads of a warp execute the same instruction. The chosen launch configuration, early     
          thread completion, and divergent flow control can significantly lower the number of active threads in a warp  
          per cycle. This workload achieves an average of 32.0 threads being active per cycle. This is further reduced  
          to 19.6 threads per warp due to predication. The compiler may use predication to avoid an actual branch.      
          Instead, all instructions are scheduled, but a per-thread condition code or predicate controls which threads  
          execute the instructions. Try to avoid different execution paths within a warp when possible.

    OPT   Est. Speedup: 35.45%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 5.5 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant      
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 35.4% of the total average of 15.6 cycles between issuing two instructions.

    OPT   Est. Speedup: 36.44%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 8.3 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant      
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 36.4% of the total average of 22.7 cycles between issuing two instructions.       
    ----- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    OPT   Est. Speedup: 35.96%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 8.1 cycles being stalled waiting for a scoreboard dependency on 
          a L1TEX (local, global, surface, texture) operation. Find the instruction producing the data being waited     
          upon to identify the culprit. To reduce the number of cycles waiting on L1TEX data accesses verify the        
          memory access patterns are optimal for the target architecture, attempt to increase cache hit rates by        
          increasing data locality (coalescing), or by changing the cache configuration. Consider moving frequently

    Avg. Active Threads Per Warp                                31.93

    ---------------------------------------- ----------- ------------

    OPT   Est. Speedup: 43.41%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 10.2 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant     
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 43.4% of the total average of 23.4 cycles between issuing two instructions.       
    ----- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    OPT   Est. Speedup: 31.44%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 7.4 cycles being stalled waiting for a scoreboard dependency on 
          a L1TEX (local, global, surface, texture) operation. Find the instruction producing the data being waited     
          upon to identify the culprit. To reduce the number of cycles waiting on L1TEX data accesses verify the        
          memory access patterns are optimal for the target architecture, attempt to increase cache hit rates by        
          increasing data locality (coalescing), or by changing the cache configuration. Consider moving frequently     
          used data to shared memory. This stall type represents about 31.4% of the total average of 23.4 cycles        
          between issuing two instructions.

    OPT   Est. Speedup: 43.36%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 11.3 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant     
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 43.4% of the total average of 26.0 cycles between issuing two instructions.       
    ----- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    OPT   Est. Speedup: 31.77%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 8.3 cycles being stalled waiting for a scoreboard dependency on 
          a L1TEX (local, global, surface, texture) operation. Find the instruction producing the data being waited     
          upon to identify the culprit. To reduce the number of cycles waiting on L1TEX data accesses verify the        
          memory access patterns are optimal for the target architecture, attempt to increase cache hit rates by        
          increasing data locality (coalescing), or by changing the cache configuration. Consider moving frequently     
          used data to shared memory. This stall type represents about 31.8% of the total average of 26.0 cycles        
          between issuing two instructions.

          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 48.2% of the total average of 32.4 cycles between issuing two instructions.       
    ----- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    OPT   Est. Speedup: 30.55%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 9.9 cycles being stalled waiting for a scoreboard dependency on 
          a L1TEX (local, global, surface, texture) operation. Find the instruction producing the data being waited     
          upon to identify the culprit. To reduce the number of cycles waiting on L1TEX data accesses verify the        
          memory access patterns are optimal for the target architecture, attempt to increase cache hit rates by        
          increasing data locality (coalescing), or by changing the cache configuration. Consider moving frequently     
          used data to shared memory. This stall type represents about 30.5% of the total average of 32.4 cycles        
          between issuing two instructions.

          thread completion, and divergent flow control can significantly lower the number of active threads in a warp  
          per cycle. This workload achieves an average of 1.0 threads being active per cycle. This is further reduced

    OPT   Est. Speedup: 43.24%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 13.5 cycles being stalled waiting for a scoreboard dependency   
          on a L1TEX (local, global, surface, texture) operation. Find the instruction producing the data being waited  
          upon to identify the culprit. To reduce the number of cycles waiting on L1TEX data accesses verify the        
          memory access patterns are optimal for the target architecture, attempt to increase cache hit rates by        
          increasing data locality (coalescing), or by changing the cache configuration. Consider moving frequently     
          used data to shared memory. This stall type represents about 43.2% of the total average of 31.2 cycles        
          between issuing two instructions.                                                                             
    ----- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    OPT   Est. Speedup: 34.42%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 10.8 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant     
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 34.4% of the total average of 31.2 cycles between issuing two instructions.       
    ----- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

          on each stall reason.

          achieved if all 32 threads of a warp execute the same instruction. The chosen launch configuration, early     
          thread completion, and divergent flow control can significantly lower the number of active threads in a warp

    OPT   Est. Speedup: 48.1%                                                                                           
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 9.0 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant      
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 48.1% of the total average of 18.7 cycles between issuing two instructions.

    OPT   Est. Speedup: 44.81%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 11.8 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant     
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 44.8% of the total average of 26.3 cycles between issuing two instructions.       
    ----- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    OPT   Est. Speedup: 30.39%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 8.0 cycles being stalled waiting for a scoreboard dependency on 
          a L1TEX (local, global, surface, texture) operation. Find the instruction producing the data being waited     
          upon to identify the culprit. To reduce the number of cycles waiting on L1TEX data accesses verify the        
          memory access patterns are optimal for the target architecture, attempt to increase cache hit rates by        
          increasing data locality (coalescing), or by changing the cache configuration. Consider moving frequently     
          used data to shared memory. This stall type represents about 30.4% of the total average of 26.3 cycles        
          between issuing two instructions.

    OPT   Est. Speedup: 36.73%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 8.3 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant      
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 36.7% of the total average of 22.7 cycles between issuing two instructions.       
    ----- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

          memory access patterns are optimal for the target architecture, attempt to increase cache hit rates by        
          increasing data locality (coalescing), or by changing the cache configuration. Consider moving frequently

    OPT   Est. Speedup: 45.43%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 10.6 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant     
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 45.4% of the total average of 23.3 cycles between issuing two instructions.       
    ----- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    OPT   Est. Speedup: 47.13%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 15.6 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant     
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 47.1% of the total average of 33.1 cycles between issuing two instructions.       
    ----- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

          memory access patterns are optimal for the target architecture, attempt to increase cache hit rates by        
          increasing data locality (coalescing), or by changing the cache configuration. Consider moving frequently

          execute the instructions. Try to avoid different execution paths within a warp when possible.

    OPT   Est. Speedup: 50.42%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 7.9 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant      
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 50.4% of the total average of 15.7 cycles between issuing two instructions.

    OPT   Est. Speedup: 46.61%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 11.6 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant     
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 46.6% of the total average of 24.8 cycles between issuing two instructions.

    OPT   Est. Speedup: 46.46%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 11.5 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant     
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 46.5% of the total average of 24.8 cycles between issuing two instructions.

    OPT   Est. Speedup: 63.25%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 12.5 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant     
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 63.2% of the total average of 19.8 cycles between issuing two instructions.

          per cycle. This workload achieves an average of 1.0 threads being active per cycle. This is further reduced

    OPT   Est. Speedup: 36.21%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 7.3 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant      
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 36.2% of the total average of 20.2 cycles between issuing two instructions.       
    ----- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

          on each stall reason.

          on a L1TEX (local, global, surface, texture) operation. Find the instruction producing the data being waited  
          upon to identify the culprit. To reduce the number of cycles waiting on L1TEX data accesses verify the        
          memory access patterns are optimal for the target architecture, attempt to increase cache hit rates by        
          increasing data locality (coalescing), or by changing the cache configuration. Consider moving frequently     
          used data to shared memory. This stall type represents about 43.9% of the total average of 22.8 cycles        
          between issuing two instructions.                                                                             
    ----- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    OPT   Est. Speedup: 31.26%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 7.1 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant      
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 31.3% of the total average of 22.8 cycles between issuing two instructions.       
    ----- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    OPT   Est. Speedup: 32.43%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 5.7 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant      
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 32.4% of the total average of 17.7 cycles between issuing two instructions.

          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 47.3% of the total average of 20.6 cycles between issuing two instructions.

    OPT   Est. Speedup: 34.1%                                                                                           
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 5.3 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant      
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 34.1% of the total average of 15.5 cycles between issuing two instructions.       
    ----- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

          on each stall reason.

    OPT   Est. Speedup: 44.36%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 11.5 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant     
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 44.4% of the total average of 26.0 cycles between issuing two instructions.       
    ----- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    OPT   Est. Speedup: 30.36%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 7.9 cycles being stalled waiting for a scoreboard dependency on 
          a L1TEX (local, global, surface, texture) operation. Find the instruction producing the data being waited     
          upon to identify the culprit. To reduce the number of cycles waiting on L1TEX data accesses verify the        
          memory access patterns are optimal for the target architecture, attempt to increase cache hit rates by        
          increasing data locality (coalescing), or by changing the cache configuration. Consider moving frequently     
          used data to shared memory. This stall type represents about 30.4% of the total average of 26.0 cycles        
          between issuing two instructions.

    OPT   Est. Speedup: 44.43%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 10.3 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant     
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 44.4% of the total average of 23.2 cycles between issuing two instructions.       
    ----- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    OPT   Est. Speedup: 31.63%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 7.3 cycles being stalled waiting for a scoreboard dependency on 
          a L1TEX (local, global, surface, texture) operation. Find the instruction producing the data being waited     
          upon to identify the culprit. To reduce the number of cycles waiting on L1TEX data accesses verify the        
          memory access patterns are optimal for the target architecture, attempt to increase cache hit rates by        
          increasing data locality (coalescing), or by changing the cache configuration. Consider moving frequently     
          used data to shared memory. This stall type represents about 31.6% of the total average of 23.2 cycles        
          between issuing two instructions.

    OPT   Est. Speedup: 43.9%                                                                                           
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 11.5 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant     
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 43.9% of the total average of 26.3 cycles between issuing two instructions.       
    ----- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

          upon to identify the culprit. To reduce the number of cycles waiting on L1TEX data accesses verify the        
          memory access patterns are optimal for the target architecture, attempt to increase cache hit rates by        
          increasing data locality (coalescing), or by changing the cache configuration. Consider moving frequently

    OPT   Est. Speedup: 41.58%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 10.3 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant     
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 41.6% of the total average of 24.8 cycles between issuing two instructions.       
    ----- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    OPT   Est. Speedup: 47.17%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 11.6 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant     
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 47.2% of the total average of 24.5 cycles between issuing two instructions.

    Section: Warp State Statistics

    ---------------------------------------- ----------- ------------
    Warp Cycles Per Issued Instruction             cycle        24.45
    Warp Cycles Per Executed Instruction           cycle        27.84
    Avg. Active Threads Per Warp                                31.42
    Avg. Not Predicated Off Threads Per Warp                    29.68
    ---------------------------------------- ----------- ------------

    OPT   Est. Speedup: 46.57%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 11.4 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant     
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 46.6% of the total average of 24.4 cycles between issuing two instructions.       
    ----- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    INF   Check the Warp Stall Sampling (All Samples) table for the top stall locations in your source based on         
          sampling data. The Kernel Profiling Guide

    Avg. Active Threads Per Warp                                31.92

    ---------------------------------------- ----------- ------------

    OPT   Est. Speedup: 34.27%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 5.3 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant      
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 34.3% of the total average of 15.3 cycles between issuing two instructions.       
    ----- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

          on each stall reason.

    OPT   Est. Speedup: 47.04%                                                                                          
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 11.6 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant     
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 47.0% of the total average of 24.6 cycles between issuing two instructions.

          On average, each warp of this workload spends 10.0 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant     
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 48.1% of the total average of 20.8 cycles between issuing two instructions.

    OPT   Est. Speedup: 37.7%                                                                                           
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 7.5 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant      
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 37.7% of the total average of 19.9 cycles between issuing two instructions.

          upon to identify the culprit. To reduce the number of cycles waiting on L1TEX data accesses verify the        
          memory access patterns are optimal for the target architecture, attempt to increase cache hit rates by        
          increasing data locality (coalescing), or by changing the cache configuration. Consider moving frequently     
          used data to shared memory. This stall type represents about 42.6% of the total average of 22.9 cycles

    ----- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    OPT   Est. Speedup: 31.4%                                                                                           
          On average, each warp of this workload spends 7.2 cycles being stalled waiting for an immediate constant      
          cache (IMC) miss. A read from constant memory costs one memory read from device memory only on a cache miss;  
          otherwise, it just costs one read from the constant cache. Immediate constants are encoded into the SASS      
          instruction as 'c[bank][offset]'. Accesses to different addresses by threads within a warp are serialized,    
          thus the cost scales linearly with the number of unique addresses read by all threads within a warp. As       
          such, the constant cache is best when threads in the same warp access only a few distinct locations. If all   
          threads of a warp access the same location, then constant memory can be as fast as a register access. This    
          stall type represents about 31.4% of the total average of 22.9 cycles between issuing two instructions.
